flags: Prophetic quote attributed to 'President Dallin H. Oaks' with talk title 'The Woman Question' dated May 1975 — title is broad/thematic and the attribution title 'President' is anachronistic for 1975 (Dallin H. Oaks was not a General Authority in 1975; he was president of BYU and was not sustained to the Quorum of the Twelve until 1984). A May 1975 general conference talk under this attribution is highly suspect and may be fabricated or misattributed.
Quote content is aphoristic and unsourced beyond month/year; no Ensign/Liahona volume, page, or session detail provided to verify.

Cross-reference Proverbs 10:24-25 connection quotes text ('The desire of the righteous shall be granted... but the substance of the wicked shall perish') that blends language across verses; Proverbs 10:25 reads 'as the whirlwind passeth, so is the wicked no more: but the righteous is an everlasting foundation.' The rendered quotation does not match the cited verses closely enough and may be paraphrased or invented.
Cross-reference Ruth 3:11 is described as 'a woman of virtue'; KJV reads 'a virtuous woman.' Minor, but quotation is not exact.
Cross-reference Proverbs 22:29 connection introduces the phrase 'woman of valor' and a claim about 'public recognition' that is an interpretive extension rather than a direct textual link.
